title.narrative: Strengthening emergency protection services through prevention and response to Gender based violence and Child protection risks to communities

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-size: 11pt text-align: justify"gtThe analysis reveals several pressing needs in Beledweyne, particularly among internally displaced persons (IDPs), focusing on child protection and gender-based violence (GBV). In the specific context of Beledweyne, the CCCM service monitoring indicated that GBV and Child protection services were lacking in the majority of IDP camps, especially after relocations following May floods. This disruption affected essential services like one-stop centers and case management facilities.lt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify"gtltspan style="font-size:11.0pt"gtThe conditions of IDPs in Beledweyne and especially in the targeted areas have given rise to worrying humanitarian indicators across social sectors including the protection sector especially Child protection and Gender based Violence. Key protection risks/concerns reported during the floods in may include an upsurge in incidences of gender-based violence and separation of children from their caregivers, HIWA has been working in Beledweyne providing GBV and supporting unaccompanied and separated children through Identification, Documentation Tracing Reunification and case management services.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify"gtltspan style="font-size:11.0pt"gtThere is a crucial need to scale up, Strengthen and sustain the provision of comprehensive case management, psychosocial support, interim care and tracing services for vulnerable women and children, supported by the strong community mechanisms, community representation and empowerment structures in order to enhance community-based structures.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style=""gtHIWA proposes an integrated child protection and gender-based violence interventions to address the most urgent and critical protection issues in Beledweyne focusing primarily on IDPs. ltspan style="text-align: left text-decoration-color: initial"gtThe project will ult/spangtltspan style="border-color: inherit outline-color: initial vertical-align: top text-align: left text-decoration-color: initial"gttilize mobile teams to reach remote areas, ensuring comprehensive service delivery and support emergency referrals from flood affected areas.lt/spangt
lt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify"gtltspan style="font-size:11.0pt"gtThe project will significantly strengthen and considerably scale –up the on-going case management response services (currently in 4 different locations in Beledweyne, i.e., 3 Case management centers and one stop center) in targeted communities. Specifically, the project will respond by identifying and responding the needs of the GBV survivors, through the provision of multi-sectoral services including case management, Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) etc. access tailored material assistance and basic emotional support.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justify"gtltspan style="font-size:11.0pt"gtWhile separated and unaccompanied children (UASC) through the provision of psychological first aid as part of the first line emergency response, interim community-based care arrangement /foster care, cash support etc. HIWA will also lead in mainstreaming child protection to other service providers to ensure compassionate, confidential, and competent action for children in emergencies. HIWA will collaborate extensively with coordination entities, including Child Protection (CP) and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) Areas of Responsibility (AORs), as well as working groups in Beledweyne district, to advance advocacy efforts and garner increased backing for the welfare and protection of children.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
lt/pgtltp style=""gtHIWA's proposed protection programming presents a robust and well-justified intervention in addressing the identified needs, particularly in child protection in emergencies (CPIE) and gender-based violence (GBV). The project plan to reach ltspan lang="EN" style="line-height: 115% border-color: windowtext"gt13,097 (3,304 Women, 3,675 girls, 2,675 men, 3,443 boys) direct beneficiaries.lt/spangtlt/pgt
